page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.16xlarge belongs to the High Clock Speed instance family, built for workloads requiring sustained processor execution speed. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the server is powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors running at a 3.4 GHz clock frequency. It provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs matched with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware GPU acceleration is not included in this configuration.

The network interface delivers a baseline throughput of 36 Gbps, accommodating high-volume communications between cluster nodes and external services. The instance features no local storage and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because local NVMe disks are absent, all operating system files and runtime persistence must be hosted on remote network storage, isolating compute resources from persistent state.

The hardware configuration emphasizes processing capability over memory capacity and local disk caching. This structure ensures that compute-bound tasks avoid the expense of unneeded memory allocations. As a result, the ecs.hfc9i.16xlarge is appropriate for compute-heavy workloads such as code compilation pipelines, continuous integration runners, high-throughput batch processing, rendering, and scientific computation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the High Clock Speed family, operating on the KVM hypervisor. Driven by x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors clocked at 3.4 GHz, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The server delivers a baseline network throughput of 36 Gbps and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. It contains no onboard GPUs and provides no local drive storage, requiring external block storage for persistent filesystem management. By focusing hardware resources on raw processor frequency rather than large memory arrays or integrated disk arrays, the server maximizes throughput per CPU core. The instance is suited for compute-heavy workloads including distributed batch computing, software build environments, scientific simulation, video transcoding, and front-end web server fleets.
